images.title: On either side of one half
images.purpose: Show 5/12 just left of 1/2 and 7/10 to the right of 1/2 on one number line from 0 to 1, so 1/2 acts as a signpost and 5/12 < 7/10.
images.composition: A number line from 0 to 1 with 1/2 as the tall signpost tick, two dots above it with their fractions, two arrows below saying less than 1/2 and more than 1/2, and the comparison at the bottom.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. One thin dark #2B2B2B horizontal number line at y 330 from x 188 to x 1268, with exactly 3 vertical ticks at x 228, 728 and 1228 (positions 0, 1/2 and 1, 1000 px for the whole). The ticks at 0 and 1 are 50 px tall; the tick at 1/2 is taller (70 px) and reddish purple #CC79A7. Under the ticks the labels 0, 1/2 and 1 (44 px, bold, dark #1F2937, about y 400). Exactly 2 dots (30 px across) on the line: a teal #0072B2 dot at x 645 (the position of 5/12, just left of 1/2) and an amber #E69F00 dot at x 928 (the position of 7/10, between 1/2 and 1). Above each dot its fraction in bold dark numerals (60 px, about y 230): 5/12 above the teal dot and 7/10 above the amber dot. Under the line, about y 470, 2 straight arrows 6 px thick with arrowheads: a teal arrow from x 718 to x 238 pointing left with the text less than 1/2 centred at x 478 under it (40 px, about y 520), and an amber arrow from x 738 to x 1218 pointing right with the text more than 1/2 centred at x 978 under it (40 px, about y 520). Across the bottom centre, about y 700, one line of bold dark text, 5/12 < 7/10 (80 px), the largest text in the frame. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
5/12 drawn to the right of 1/2 or 7/10 to the left of 1/2
any tick or label other than 0, 1/2 and 1
images.takeaway: 5/12 is less than 1/2 and 7/10 is more than 1/2, so 5/12 < 7/10.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 1 with 5/12 marked just left of 1/2 and 7/10 marked right of 1/2, arrows saying less than 1/2 and more than 1/2, and 5/12 < 7/10 written below.
images.context: Concept image for Less Than Half, More Than Half. It follows the idea of the figure in your maths book (fractions placed on a number line with 1/2 as the reference) and shows the concept's own example, 5/12 and 7/10.
images.teaching_notes: Ask which side of 1/2 each fraction sits on, using half of the bottom number (6 for 12, 5 for 10). The slip to watch is thinking that the bigger bottom number, 12, makes the bigger fraction.

image_decisions.why: A number line with 5/12 left of 1/2 and 7/10 right of 1/2 is the whole reasoning of comparing with the reference 1/2.
